name: UI/UX review
description: Read-only review of usability, accessibility and visual hierarchy. Two reviewers reconcile findings in up to 4 rounds. Supply screenshots or access to the UI; code alone cannot establish a visual verdict.

steps.name: Inspect the interface independently
steps.promptTemplate:
Review the supplied interface for usability, accessibility, navigation, reading hierarchy, spacing, responsiveness, focus and action feedback. Inspect the available code and screenshots. Do not edit files. Distinguish observed defects from unverified hypotheses. State which screens, widths and interactions you actually inspected. If no graphical evidence or interface access is available, report the visual acceptance gap; do not invent a visual verdict.

{{userPrompt}}

steps.name: Reconcile UI/UX findings
steps.promptTemplate:
Carefully cross-reference the other participant's complete answer with repository evidence. Return JSON only with candidate, accepted, objections, and unresolvedRisks. candidate must be {"summary":"...","findings":[...]}. summary must be a concise user-facing review report explaining what converged, what was rejected, what remains unresolved, and why, using only recorded evidence. Distinguish disagreement from missing evidence. Do not invent agreement or turn unresolved findings into confirmed defects. Agreement with an exact candidate means agreement with its recorded dispositions, including any unresolved ones. Keep the report and every finding consistent; a participant's conclusion is not unanimous consensus. Each finding needs stable id, subject, message, explicit disposition accepted/rejected/unresolved, evidence and challenges string arrays, optional severity error/warning/information, and optional location with file/startLine/endLine. accepted is boolean for this exact candidate. Keep proposed claims out of accepted findings.
